text:
B: Alright! There she is. Can you hear me, love?
A: Yeah. Gemma.
B: Darren. Nice to meet you. Third one of these for me, I'm getting good at it now.
A: Same. Is this the last one?
B: Dunno, mate. I just do what the screen tells me.
A: Fair enough. Where are you?
B: Bridgwater, Somerset. Born and bred. You?
A: Huntingdon. Cambridgeshire.
B: Never been. Is it nice?
A: It's alright. It's got a Tesco.
B: Ha! Sold me. So what do you do, then? You look like you've come straight from work, with the fleece.
A: Yeah, I have. Site ops manager at a distribution centre. Warehouse, basically. About a hundred and eighty staff.
B: No way. I was on forklifts, me. Distribution centre off the M5, years. Counterbalance mostly.
A: Yeah? Where are you now, then?
B: Er, nowhere at the minute. Did my back in. Signed off about eighteen months ago, so I'm on the Universal Credit, seeing a work coach every couple of weeks, the whole lot. Looking at lighter stuff, van driving maybe, or caretaker at a school. Not much call for a forklift driver who can't twist round, do you know what I mean?
A: Mm. You could do a lot worse than security. We're always short of gatehouse.
B: Yeah, that's on the list.
A: Get your CV in early, though, don't wait for it to come to you. I've had blokes on the jobcentre scheme send me a CV with three years missing and no explanation. It just goes in the bin, sorry, but it does.
B: Right. Well, I'd put "back knackered" in mine, so you'd know.
A: That's not what I meant.
B: No, I know, I know. It's just everyone's got advice, you know. The work coach, the wife, the bloke in the pub. Sorry, I'm going off on one. It gets to you a bit.
A: ...Yeah. Fair. My dad was a lorry driver. Did his back about four times. He's not great now, health-wise.
B: Oh, sorry to hear that. Is he local to you?
A: St Neots. Twenty minutes. I should go more than I do.
B: Go when you can, love. Lost my mum six years back, you don't get them back, do you.
A: No. ...Anyway. What's that on your top, Bristol City?
B: Bristol City, yeah. Loosely. Bridgwater United properly. You into it?
A: Not really. Husband's Arsenal. I just hear him shouting at the telly.
B: Arsenal. Poor sod. There's another bloke in this lot, the computer one, I bet he's Arsenal an' all.
A: He is. I've had him. He was gaming on his lunch break at four o'clock.
B: Ha! Good for him, to be fair.
A: I'd have sacked him.
B: I bet you would. You've got that look, you have. No offence.
A: None taken. I get it a lot.
B: What do you do for fun, then, when you're not sacking people?
A: Walk the dog. Telly. Gin. Tenerife once a year if I can get Craig to book it.
B: Tenerife! Been twice. Best holidays I ever had, I'm telling you. Pool, bit of sun, pint at eleven in the morning, nobody looking at you funny—
A: That's it. That's all I want. Sunbed and nobody ringing me abou—
